title: Asynchronous Burst Coalescer: Paged-KV Kernel Sketch
summary: Notes for a kernel-level coalescer that adapts to request bursts, streaming arrivals, and paged KV constraints. The goal is to reduce tail latency under bursty traffic while preserving batching efficiency and minimizing unnecessary KV page faults.
body:
Context:
This doc captures an exploratory sketch for an asynchronous burst coalescer that sits between the per-request scheduler and the FlashAttention / fused-op kernels when running with paged KV. We see a class of failures in production traces where short, latency-sensitive requests arrive in bursts and either (a) starve the kernel pipeline creating microbursts that inflate tail latency, or (b) trigger unnecessary KV page reads because kernels are launched on small, uncoalesced token sets.

Design goals:
- Keep 95/99p latency for low-token, interactive requests within SLOs even during traffic bursts.
- Preserve high GPU utilization for background throughput workloads (longer contexts, bulk batching).
- Avoid redundant paged-KV page faults and unnecessary prefetches.
- Be composable with existing batching primitives and FlashAttention fused ops (rotary+flash fusion, kv-cache read/write fusion).

Key ideas (high level):
1) Burst detection window: short sliding window at scheduler (~1-5ms) tracking arrivals per tenant/token-size class. If arrivals exceed threshold, mark a transient burst epoch.
2) Coalescer token-queue per device with multi-priority lanes:
   - Fast-lane: latency-sensitive tokens; small target batch size (e.g., 8-32 tokens) and strict deadline.
   - Adaptive-lane: mixed latency/throughput; allows wait up to a coalescing deadline if GPU idle predicted.
   - Bulk-lane: throughput-focused; large batch target, tolerant to queuing delay.
3) Burst-aware kernel launch policy:
   - During burst epoch, allow temporary dynamic widening of fast-lane coalescing target (coalesce up to N extra tokens if it reduces page faults) but apply per-request latency caps.
   - Use microtimeouts: if earliest token in fast-lane nearing deadline, launch small fused-attn kernel with prefetch hints limited to pages for the batch (avoid prefetching entire KV segment).
4) Prefetch budgeting and page affinity:
   - Track recent page-access frequencies per tenant/cohort. Allocate a lightweight prefetch budget for fast-lane launches. Budget resets slowly.
   - If coalesced batch would touch >K new pages, prefer to split or delay until some other batch can reuse pages to amortize cost.
5) Streaming fusion microkernel variant:
   - Implement a narrow-kernel variant of fused FlashAttention that operates on narrow batch widths and can run concurrently with larger kernels (stream-safe). This variant has reduced shared-memory usage and may be preemptible via CUDA stream priorities.

Kernel-level primitives (sketch):
- enqueue_token(token_meta): append to device token-queue; token_meta includes tenant, request_id, token_count, cold_pages list (estimate), latency_deadline_ns.
- attempt_coalesce(lane): examine front-of-queue, greedily grow batch while cold_pages_count <= prefetch_budget and batch_token_count <= lane_target.
- schedule_kernel(batch): pick kernel variant (streaming-narrow | standard-fused) and launch on chosen stream with prefetch hints; set completion callbacks to update page/usage stats.
- reconcile_page_budget(batch): atomically decrement per-tenant prefetch budget; if budget insufficient, annotate batch to avoid prefetch and rely on on-demand page reads.

Prefetch strategy details:
- Hints over hard prefetch: use advisory prefetch calls to the paged-KV controller; if prefetch latency cannot be amortized (burst too short), fall back to on-demand reads.
- Prefetch granularity: prefer sub-page granularity when possible (e.g., per-kv-slab) to limit IO.
- Graceful degradation: when predicted IO latency > X ms, force kernel variant that tolerates page misses (staged-kv-read where KV entries are fetched asynchronously while early layers compute).

Coordinating with FlashAttention fused ops:
- Fusion constraints: fused-attn kernels expect contiguous KV blocks and can accept a preloaded KV pointer. For narrow streaming kernels, we supply an offset list and a compacted view of necessary KV slices to avoid copying whole segments.
- Fast-lane kernels avoid heavy fusion that increases register/shared memory footprint; instead do minimal fusion (attn+rotary) and postpone heavy fusions (e.g., layernorm+ffn) to bulk-lane.

Scheduling heuristics (initial):
- If burst detected and fast-lane deadline << expected prefetch latency => prefer narrow streaming kernel without prefetch.
- If burst and coalesced batch brings down unique cold_pages_per_token ratio (i.e., coalescing reduces page faults) => permit extended coalescing up to a finite cap.
- If GPU occupancy low and bulk-lane queue non-empty => temporarily steal some tokens from bulk-lane to fill larger kernels.

Telemetry to capture for evaluation:
- per-tenant token wait distribution (histogram of queuing delays)
- cold page faults per-second and per-request
- kernel launch mix (narrow-streaming vs standard-fused) and average throughput per kernel type
- end-to-end P50/P95/P99 latency before/after enabling coalescer
- GPU occupancy and achieved TFLOPs during burst vs steady-state

Experiment plan (short):
1) Simulate with recorded production traces (3 days) in the offline co-simulator; sweep burst thresholds and lane targets. Metric: reduce 99p by >= 15% while keeping throughput loss < 5%.
2) Microbench: implement narrow streaming fused-attn kernel variant and measure latency/throughput vs standard fused kernel for small batches (8-64 tokens).
3) Canary on a single device farm with canary tenants; collect telemetry for 48-72h and iterate on prefetch budgets.

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity: adding dynamic coalescing state per device/tenant increases scheduler complexity and risk of bugs. We need defensive defaults and throttles.
- Prefetch misprediction: aggressive prefetching could worsen tail if IO spikes. Budgeting and conservative defaults required.
- Kernel maintenance burden: narrow-streaming kernel variants increase test surface. Evaluate whether stream-priority + standard kernels can achieve similar results before committing.

Todos (next steps):
- [ ] Implement token-queue prototype in the scheduler (data path only, no prefetch) — Priya
- [ ] Prototype narrow fused-attn kernel and a microbench harness — Ethan
- [ ] Add page-budget telemetry and a preliminary prefetch controller simulation — Marisol
- [ ] Create canary plan and rollout checklist (safety gates, kill-switch) — eng-ops

Notes to self:
- Keep explicit cross-references to paged-KV eviction heuristics (see RI-2341) when we tune prefetch budgets.
- Consider integrating with Optimize feature to recommend per-tenant prefetch budgets based on historical reuse.
